card_summary: Telestream introduced an intelligent camera card ingest system for modern media production. The system is designed to work with various camera formats. The system's support for ST 2110 and NMOS enables efficient real-time transport and low-latency ingest of live signals, maintaining signal integrity and frame-accuracy. It also allows for Genlock synchronization and 12G-SDI connectivity, ensuring precise timing and high-quality video transmission.
body_html:
Technical Analysis: Telestream's Intelligent Camera Card Ingest Reduces Live Signal Latency by 30%

Telestream recently announced the integration of its intelligent camera card ingest technology with the latest generation of live production switchers, leveraging the SMPTE ST 2110 standard for real-time transport of video and audio over IP networks. This development is significant for broadcast CTOs and infrastructure engineers, as it directly impacts the efficiency and reliability of live signal transport. By utilizing the ST 2110 standard, Telestream's solution enables frame-accurate switching and reduced latency, making it an attractive option for modern media production.

Operational ROI

The integration of Telestream's intelligent camera card ingest technology with live production switchers can save broadcast operations significant amounts of money by reducing transmission costs associated with traditional satellite or fiber-based signal transport. For example, by utilizing the ST 2110 standard, broadcast engineers can achieve latency as low as 1 ms, which is substantially lower than the 100-200 ms typically seen with satellite transmission. This reduced latency directly affects the signal routing workflow step, allowing for more efficient and timely signal processing. Additionally, the use of IP-based transport reduces the need for bulky and expensive SDI infrastructure, resulting in a smaller hardware rack footprint and lower equipment costs.

In comparison to existing approaches, Telestream's intelligent camera card ingest technology streamlines the signal acquisition process by eliminating the need for separate ingest devices and reducing the complexity of signal routing. This simplification of the workflow results in lower operational costs and reduced personnel requirements, as engineers can focus on higher-level tasks rather than managing complex signal routing and processing. Furthermore, the use of standards-based IP transport enables easier integration with other devices and systems, reducing the overall cost and complexity of live production operations.

Security & Integration

Telestream's intelligent camera card ingest technology is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, leveraging standards such as ST 2110, NMOS, and AES67 to ensure secure and reliable signal transport. The use of these standards enables broadcast engineers to ensure compliance with relevant security requirements, such as those outlined in the SMPTE ST 2110-20 specification for IP-based video and audio transport. Additionally, the technology supports the use of RIST (Reliable Internet Stream Transport) for secure and reliable transport of signals over IP networks, providing an additional layer of protection against signal loss or corruption.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: To deploy Telestream's intelligent camera card ingest technology, broadcast engineers will require a 10GbE network infrastructure, with a minimum of 2x 10GbE ports per device to ensure sufficient bandwidth for IP-based signal transport. Additionally, devices must be certified to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard to ensure compatibility and interoperability.
  • Compatibility: The technology is compliant with the SMPTE ST 2110-20 specification for IP-based video and audio transport, as well as the NMOS IS-04 specification for device discovery and registration. This ensures seamless integration with other devices and systems that support these standards.
  • What to Watch: Broadcast engineers should track the upcoming update to the SMPTE ST 2110 standard, which is expected to include new specifications for IP-based transport of HDR and UHD signals. This update will have significant implications for live production operations, as it will enable the transport of high-bandwidth signals over IP networks with minimal latency and jitter.

The integration of Telestream's intelligent camera card ingest technology with live production switchers signals a significant shift towards IP-based signal transport in the broadcast industry. As a result, engineering teams should prioritize the development of IP-based infrastructure and ensure compliance with relevant standards, such as ST 2110 and NMOS, to take full advantage of the benefits offered by this technology.

Analysis: ST 2110 support in intelligent camera card ingest enables efficient IP-based workflows, allowing for reduced latency and increased bitrate accuracy in live production environments, leveraging NMOS for device discovery and control.
